drafted_from: tool:listen-to-a-generated-voice-take-word-by-word's own row (its words, invoke, input and output schema) in tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json; it runs on the person's computer and has no sample run here, so this kit is a draft until a real run's answer is put in
start_here: Say to your AI: "Listen to my voice take /Work/demo/take.wav word by word with its word times /Work/demo/take.words.json and tell me which words sound least like a warm, calm narrator." It runs tool:listen-to-a-generated-voice-take-word-by-word on your computer and writes each word's scores to /Work/demo/take.listen.json.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a take and its word times on your computer and writes the JSON file you name.
instructions: 1. Install python3, numpy and the earshot listening package, and clone the Workshop (git clone https://github.com/Trillion-X/trillion-workshop.git).

2. Your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its run command on your computer: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/grade-and-repair-speech-audio/do-work/listen_voice_take_words.py /Work/demo/take.wav /Work/demo/take.words.json 0 /Work/demo/take.listen.json "a warm, calm narrator"
3. Read take.listen.json: the words with the lowest realness and the highest glitch match are the ones to regenerate.

worked_examples.title: One take heard word by word
worked_examples.ask: Which words of this take sound least real?
worked_examples.given: A text-to-speech take /Work/demo/take.wav, its word times /Work/demo/take.words.json and the voice wanted "a warm, calm narrator".
